C05-M01-L08-F1.title: Penetration-test report structure by audience
C05-M01-L08-F1.caption: A report is layered from the leadership decision at the top to raw supporting evidence at the bottom, each layer written for a specific reader.
C05-M01-L08-F1.alt: Stack of seven layers, top first: Executive summary (leadership: risk, impact, recommendation), highlighted dark; Scope, methodology, limitations (auditors: authorised, how, what not); Summary of findings (CISO: ID, severity, status); Detailed findings (engineers: evidence, CVSS, fix, retest), highlighted orange; Remediation roadmap (owners: prioritised actions); Retest results (everyone: closed or still open); Appendices (raw output, captures, hash manifest).
C05-M01-L08-F1.note: Each layer summarises the ones beneath it; readers stop when they have what they need.

C05-M01-L08-F2.title: The lab reporting pipeline: from verification to retest
C05-M01-L08-F2.caption: Confirmed evidence is scored and ranked into a report, the client remediates, and a retest with the same checks closes each finding.
C05-M01-L08-F2.alt: Top-to-bottom flow of seven steps: verify.py (minimum safe check per finding); data/findings.json (confirmed findings + UTC time); report.py + cvss.py (score, rank, attach fix and retest); Report delivered (executive summary + findings); Client remediates (fix the root cause); retest.py --port 8100 (same checks, hardened target); Retest results (4 of 4 closed), highlighted as the outcome. A loop arrow from the last step back to the start is labelled: open findings return for further remediation.

steps.label: report.py + cvss.py
steps.sub: score, rank, attach fix and retest

loop.label: open findings return for further remediation

C05-M01-L08-F2.note: A finding is closed by evidence from a retest, not by assertion.
